title: What If All of Earth's Water Were One Giant Ball?

scenes.text: What if all of Earth's water became one ball? It's far smaller than you'd guess.
Oceans, lakes, rivers, ice and clouds together make about 332 million cubic miles of water.
Squeeze it into a sphere and it's roughly 860 miles across.
That's a tiny blue dot next to the planet it came from.
Earth is 7,900 miles wide, so the ball would be a fraction of its width.
The deep ocean feels endless, but on a planet scale it's a thin film.

description:
What if all of Earth's water became one ball?
All the water on the planet would form a sphere only about 860 miles wide.
What should we run through next?
